title: Understand widening and narrowing type casting in Java
answer: Type casting in Java means converting a value from one type to another. Primitive numeric conversions are commonly divided into widening and narrowing conversions. Widening conversions, such as `int` to `long`, generally happen implicitly because the destination can represent the source range without the same risk of information loss. Narrowing conversions, such as `double` to `int` or `int` to `byte`, require an explicit cast because information may be discarded or the value may wrap. Reference types also support casting within compatible inheritance relationships, with invalid runtime casts potentially causing `ClassCastException`. In AeroTopo's `LanguageLab.numericConversions`, `(int) metres` truncates the fractional part, `(byte) truncated` can wrap, and assigning the int to a long demonstrates widening.

steps.title: Focus on double to int narrowing
steps.question: Casting `double metres` to `int` explicitly narrows the value because an integer cannot preserve the fractional component of a floating-point number. What information is lost when `(int) metres` converts a value such as `258.9` into the local variable `truncated`?
steps.why: The fractional portion is discarded, producing 258 rather than rounding the value.
steps.why_te: Highlight ayina line ni chudandi. `(int) metres` narrowing conversion fractional `.9` part ni discard chestundi. `258.9` value `258` ga truncate avutundi.

steps.title: Focus on int to byte narrowing
steps.question: Narrowing to byte keeps only the low-order bits, so values outside the byte range wrap according to Java's numeric conversion rules. The next conversion casts the integer value into an eight-bit `byte`, whose numeric range is much smaller than `int`. Why can `(byte) truncated` change `258` into a seemingly unrelated value instead of simply preserving 258?
steps.why: Narrowing to byte keeps only the low-order bits, so values outside the byte range wrap according to Java's numeric conversion rules.
steps.why_te: Highlight ayina line ni chudandi. `byte` range small kabatti 258 direct ga represent cheyyaledu. Narrowing cast low-order bits ni retain chestundi, result wrap ayi test lo `2` ga kanipistundi.

steps.title: Focus on int to long widening
steps.question: Assigning the same `int` value into a `long` does not require an explicit cast because the destination type has a wider integral range. Why is `long widened = truncated` considered a widening conversion and normally safe from this kind of range loss?
steps.why: Every int value can be represented as a long value, so Java permits the conversion implicitly.
steps.why_te: Highlight ayina line ni chudandi. `long` range `int` kanna wider kabatti every int value long lo represent cheyyachu. Anduke `long widened = truncated` implicit widening conversion.
